State { get; set; }\\n```\\n\\n##### Property Value\\n\\nstring\\n\\n##### Remarks\\n\\nIf the state is `ENABLED` , then the compute environment accepts jobs from a queue and can scale out automatically based on queues.\\n\\nIf the state is `ENABLED` , then the AWS Batch scheduler can attempt to place jobs from an associated job queue on the compute resources within the environment. Jobs in a `STARTING` or `RUNNING` state continue to progress normally. Managed compute environments in the `DISABLED` state don't scale out.\\n\\n```\\nCompute environments in a DISABLED state may continue to incur billing charges. State { get; set; }\\n```\\n\\n##### Property Value\\n\\nstring\\n\\n##### Remarks\\n\\nIf the state is `ENABLED` , then the compute environment accepts jobs from a queue and can scale out automatically based on queues.\\n\\nIf the state is `ENABLED` , then the AWS Batch scheduler can attempt to place jobs from an associated job queue on the compute resources within the environment. If the compute environment is managed, then it can scale its instances out or in automatically, based on the job queue demand.\\n\\nIf the state is `DISABLED` , then the AWS Batch scheduler doesn't attempt to place jobs within the environment. For example, consider a `c5.8xlarge` instance with a `minvCpus` value of `4` and a `desiredvCpus` value of `36` . This instance doesn't scale down to a `c5.large` instance.\\n\\n**See**: http://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/aws-resource-batch-computeenvironment.html#cfn-batch-computeenvironment-state\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cdk/api/v2/dotnet/api/Amazon.CDK.AWS.Batch.CfnComputeEnvironmentProps.html\"},{\"rank_order\":3,\"title\":\"How do I fix a compute environment that's not valid in AWS Batch?\",\"context\":\"### \\\"CLIENT\\\\_ERROR - Your compute environment has been INVALIDATED and scaled down\\\" error\\n\\nWhen AWS Batch scales out a compute environment, the container instances join the Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster. If the instances can't join the cluster, then AWS Batch marks the compute environment as **INVALID**. This occurs when the Amazon ECS agent on the instance doesn't call the **RegisterContainerInstance** API within an established time frame. In response, AWS Batch terminates the instance, and you receive the following error:\\n\\n\\\"CLIENT\\\\_ERROR - Your compute environment has been INVALIDATED and scaled down\\\" because none of the instances joined the underlying ECS Cluster.\\\"\\n\\nYour instances can't join an Amazon ECS cluster in the following scenarios:\\n\\n* Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC) [subnet configuration](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/configure-subnets.html) settings prevent successful communication with Amazon ECS.\\n* An incorrect instance profile policy setting prevents authorization to Amazon ECS.\\n* Custom [Amazon Machine Images](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/AMIs.html) (AMIs) or [launch template](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/launch-templates.html) configurations affect the Amazon ECS agent.\\n\\nTo troubleshoot this issue, complete the following steps:\\n\\n1. Open the [AWS Batch console](https://console.aws.amazon.com/batch/).\\n2. In the navigation pane, choose **Compute environments**.\\n3. Select the compute environment that's in the INVALID state. Then, choose **Disable**.\\n4. Select the same compute environment, and then choose **Enable**.\\n\\nThe preceding steps reactivate the compute environment and cause AWS Batch to mark the environment as VALID. To launch one instance and force a scale out, update the **minVcpus** parameter to **1**. Then, use the running instance to [troubleshoot the reason that instances can't join the Amazon ECS cluster](https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/ecs-instance-unable-join-cluster)\",\"url\":\"https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/batch-invalid-compute-environment\"}]}}"}]}], "label": "Verifying against published AWS documentation"}
